producer_report.summary: Added three standing defaults (outcome-check, no-empty-success, thrash-stop) to defaults.toml, each applying to every class, each citing this job in its source. The reader prompt now has one line telling the reader to record applicable standing defaults as acceptance criteria and not to ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise. Tests show that a docs request ("write an explainer page") receives all three. Enforcement is prose-only: no loop code computes the 4-of-5 rating or detects thrashing, and the statements, changelog and design doc say so. The reader's token set went over its 2,000 budget, so I trimmed wording elsewhere in reader.md. I did not raise the budget, because the file that holds it is not a deliverable.

checks_run.note: All suites pass; the 1 ignored test in the athena-agent unit suite is pre-existing. The last run came after the final prompt trims and fmt.
The first check flagged one test in briefs.rs. I ran cargo fmt --all and re-ran the tests; I did not re-run the check itself afterwards.
Run before the final fmt pass and prompt trims. The last edits were prose and whitespace, and I did not re-run it.

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml gains three [[default]] entries with unique ids (outcome-check, no-empty-success, thrash-stop), each applies_to ["*"] (or classes that include docs), each with a source citing this request, and each statement's first sentence states the core rule, since render shows only that sentence.
criteria_check.evidence: Read defaults.toml. Three entries with applies_to ["*"] and a source naming job 20261015-095214-1egb. The first sentence of each is the core rule. The athena-data test checks the rendered lines.

criteria_check.criterion: The outcome-check statement says: the outcome is the check behind the work, not the activity; for audience-facing quality a fresh model reader that took no part in the work rates the live result as a newcomer, and a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion. no-empty-success says an empty queue or finished list never counts as success alone. thrash-stop says that if the same item fails twice in a loop, the loop stops and reports thrashing.
criteria_check.evidence: Read the statements in defaults.toml. The test asserts the outcome-check phrases 'fresh model reader that took no part in the work' and 'below 4 of 5 blocks completion'. The first sentences of no-empty-success and thrash-stop are asserted in the rendered output.

criteria_check.criterion: The reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md) tells the reader to record applicable standing defaults of this kind as acceptance criteria and not to ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise.
criteria_check.evidence: The new line in reader.md reads 'Standing defaults like outcome-check apply unasked: record each applicable one as an acceptance criterion; do not ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise.' The briefs.rs test asserts these phrases.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: a new test loads the repository defaults.toml, selects defaults for class docs (an explainer page request), and shows the three defaults appear in the rendered default list; the existing parse, duplicate and render tests still pass.
criteria_check.evidence: The new test an_explainer_page_request_gets_the_three_standing_defaults in athena-data defaults.rs selects the defaults whose applies_to includes '*' or 'docs', renders them, and asserts the three lines. It also asserts the code-only 'rust' default is absent. The full cargo test --locked passed, including the existing tests.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test` for the workspace: a new test builds the reader brief for the request 'write an explainer page' and shows it contains the three defaults and the instruction to turn them into acceptance criteria, with no question field required; a rival check shows a request that says otherwise is not forced to carry them if the reader prompt supports that wording.
criteria_check.evidence: The briefs.rs test an_explainer_page_request_gets_the_standing_defaults_without_a_question builds the reader brief for 'write an explainer page' and asserts it carries no 'Question asked'. The defaults are not in the brief itself but in the reader's system prompt, so the test also composes the contract, the reader frame and the rendered defaults. It asserts the three default lines and the instruction wording in that composed prompt. The rival check asserts the prompt contains 'unless the request says otherwise'. This checks the prompt wording only; it does not exercise a request that opts out.
cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings finished clean. cargo fmt --all was applied after the one formatting diff.

open_issues: The reader token budget in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs (2,000, D25) was exceeded by about 135 tokens, and I met it by trimming wording in reader.md instead of raising it. The next default added will hit the budget again.
Enforcement of the 4-of-5 rating and the thrash stop in loop code is not built; the defaults are marked prose-only.
mistakes: My first prompt line and first defaults pushed the reader set to 2,135 tokens, which failed the budgets test. It took several rounds of trimming to bring it under 2,000.
One test assertion was not rustfmt-clean at first; fixed with cargo fmt.
learnings: The reader's defaults reach it through its system prompt (reader.md plus defaults.render(), assembled in athena-core reading.rs). The reader brief itself carries no defaults.
render() shows only the first sentence of each statement, so that sentence is what counts against the reader token budget.
crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs fails when the reader set is over 2,000 tokens, using a bytes/3 estimate.
desires: A way to measure the reader token estimate without running the full budgets test.
